title: Canonical completed coefficient pullback comparison respects finite quotient projections
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data $p,a,q,k_0,k$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $\mathcal O_E$, $\varpi_E$ and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ ($n\ge1$) [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_{T,n}=(A_n)_T$ and $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}=\varprojlim_nB_{T,n}$ for $T=X,Y$, with projections $\pi_{n,T}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the inverse image and ring isomorphisms $c_n:g^{-1}B_{Y,n}\to B_{X,n}$ and $c_R:g^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], where $\pi_{n,X}c_R=c_ng^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})$.

Let $P_g=Lg^*$ be the completed integral pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $\kappa_{R_Y}:g^{-1}R_Y\to P_gR_Y$ be the specified map [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b). Let $\lambda_R:P_gR_Y\to g^{-1}R_Y$ be the CANONICAL multiplication/completeness comparison of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]: on a flat-term K-flat model [def-pc-kflat-complex] it is induced on the entire strict quotient cone by the finite maps $x\otimes b\mapsto c_n^{-1}(b)x$, the inverse-image comparison for that cone, and the inverse of the canonical completeness map. At finite level let $\lambda_n:Lg_n^*B_{Y,n}\to g^{-1}B_{Y,n}$ be $x\otimes b\mapsto c_n^{-1}(b)x$; its inverse is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. The coefficient sheaf $R_Y$ and its reductions are derived complete constructible coefficient objects [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Let $\rho_n:P_gR_Y\to\operatorname{Res}_n Lg_n^*B_{Y,n}$ be the specified projection of the completed pullback model, using the canonical reduction $R_Y\otimes^L A_n\cong B_{Y,n}$ and restriction of scalars [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].

Then the canonical comparison, including its actual cone maps, satisfies
$$\lambda_R\circ\kappa_{R_Y}=\mathrm{id}_{g^{-1}R_Y},\qquad \kappa_{R_Y}\circ\lambda_R=\mathrm{id}_{P_gR_Y},$$
$$\operatorname{Res}_n(\lambda_n)\circ\rho_n=g^{-1}(\pi_{n,Y})\circ\lambda_R,$$
and consequently, for $\theta_R=c_R\circ\lambda_R$,
$$\pi_{n,X}\circ\theta_R=\operatorname{Res}_n(c_n\circ\lambda_n)\circ\rho_n.$$
The equalities are compatible with the specified maps $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ before passing to the derived inverse limit. When $X=Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ and $g=g_Y$, this is the canonical $\lambda$ and $\theta_{\mathcal O_E}$ used in [def-weil-constant-weil-structure](3), not an arbitrary isomorphism $P_gR_Y\cong g^{-1}R_Y$. This is a statement about coefficient pullback and its reduction projections, without a claim about Frobenius on cohomology.

proof.text: The existing coefficient-model-map proofs identify finite reduction with the finite regular-module isomorphism using the normalized scalar adjunction; the finite and integral unit maps are the sectionwise inverse coefficient maps. The finite tensor-unit map, conjugated by the regular inverse-image and pullback identifications, is identity on the regular generator. Hence the existing theorem canonicalCoefficientModelMaps_isIso supplies all the required isomorphisms.

Identify the sectionwise inverse image of the regular integral complex with the regular complex on X. Its inverse sends the unit section to the unit section. Composing this inverse with each specified inverseImageReductionTheta gives pullbackUnitLevel: check the defining theta formula on the regular generator, use the reduction tensor formula and naturality of pullbackUnitSections along the comma arrow. The zero shifted component and the actual product projections then identify its Roos augmentation with constantWeilChainUnit. Exact single-complex/derived comparisons transport this identity to canonicalCoefficientKappa = c_R composed with the inverse of constantWeilIntegralRoosComparison. The definition of canonicalCoefficientLambda is the reverse composite. Cancellation gives both inverse identities and the published theta normalization.

At finite level the existing tensor-unit triangle implies that lambda_n followed by c_n equals coefficientFinitePullIso.hom. The canonical reduction complex is finiteSingleRegularIso.hom. Their composite after pullbackUnitLevel is the actual coefficient projection, by pullbackLevelRegularIso_projection and the exact restriction/single comparison. Precompose rho_n with the inverse normalized Roos comparison: the chain unit followed by the actual first cone coordinate and nth product projection equals pullbackUnitLevel. Localize this chain equality. It gives the theta projection identity; postcompose with the inverse finite coefficient comparison to obtain the lambda projection identity.

The coefficient projection followed by inverse canonical reduction sends its regular unit section to constantWeilReducedUnitSection, since finiteSingleRegularIso sends that section to one. The specified unrestrictedIntegralTransition sends this reduced unit to the next reduced unit. The regular-source extensionality lemma therefore proves compatibility of the actual coefficient projections with canonicalCoefficientTransition. These coefficient projections are epimorphisms: quotientProjection_epi and single-complex extensionality reduce cancellation to degree zero, where the surrounding single-object identifications are isomorphisms. PullbackUnitLevel is consequently epimorphic as well. Precompose the proposed strict finite transition square with pullbackUnitLevel followed by canonical reduction, and postcompose with c_n. The finite multiplication formula, strict pullbackUnitLevel_transition, and the coefficient projection compatibility give equality. Cancel the epimorphism and the finite coefficient isomorphism. This proves the transition equality before localization.

For the derived rho transition identity, precompose with the inverse normalized Roos comparison, which is an isomorphism by constantWeilChainUnit_isIso. The preceding explicit rho equation reduces the result to pullbackUnitLevel_transition after cancelling the two consecutive canonical reduction isomorphisms. Thus the equality follows from a strict chain equation; no uniqueness assertion for morphisms from finite derived projections is required.

lean.statement: theorem canonicalCoefficientPullbackReduction (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (_hl : l ≠ D.p) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g] (hX : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (l : X.presheaf.stalk x)) (hY : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (l : Y.presheaf.stalk y)) : canonicalCoefficientKappa l E g hX hY ≫ (canonicalCoefficientLambda l E g).hom = 𝟙 _ ∧ (canonicalCoefficientLambda l E g).hom ≫ canonicalCoefficientKappa l E g hX hY = 𝟙 _ ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, canonicalCoefficientRho l E g n ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map ((canonicalCoefficientRes l E X n).map (canonicalCoefficientLambdaFinite l E g n).hom) = (canonicalCoefficientLambda l E g).hom ≫ canonicalCoefficientInverseProjection l E g n) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, (canonicalCoefficientTheta l E g).hom ≫ canonicalCoefficientProjection l E X n = canonicalCoefficientRho l E g n ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map ((canonicalCoefficientRes l E X n).map ((canonicalCoefficientLambdaFinite l E g n).hom ≫ (canonicalCoefficientFiniteComparison l E g n).hom))) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, canonicalCoefficientPullbackTransition l E g n ≫ (canonicalCoefficientRes l E X n).map (canonicalCoefficientLambdaFinite l E g n).hom = (canonicalCoefficientRes l E X (n + 1)).map (canonicalCoefficientLambdaFinite l E g (n + 1)).hom ≫ canonicalCoefficientInverseTransition l E g n) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, canonicalCoefficientRho l E g (n + 1) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (canonicalCoefficientPullbackTransition l E g n) = canonicalCoefficientRho l E g n) ∧ canonicalCoefficientTheta l E g = constantWeilIntegralTheta l E g
